findings.obs_text: The Lord or God knows the thoughts of people in Job 21:27, Psa 94:11, Psa 139:2, Psa 139:23, Eze 11:5, 1Ch 28:9, 1Cor 3:20 and 1Cor 2:11: he knows them from afar, knows the things that come into the mind, knows that they are a breath and futile; only a person's own spirit, and God's Spirit, comprehends the thoughts.
findings.grounds: you discern my thoughts from afar

findings.obs_text: Jesus knows or perceives the thoughts of those around him in Mat 9:4, Mat 12:25, Luk 5:22, Luk 6:8 and Luk 11:17, and answers them: the knowing of thoughts is his, and it leads to his word.
findings.grounds: Knowing their thoughts, he said to them

findings.obs_text: In Mic 4:12 the nations do not know the Lord's thoughts, and in Dan 2:29 and Dan 2:30 the king's thoughts are made known by the revealer of mysteries: the thoughts of God are not known except as he makes them known.
findings.grounds: they do not know the thoughts of the Lord

findings.obs_text: In Exo 2:14, Rut 4:4, 1Sa 20:3, 2Ki 7:12, Act 12:9, Rom 1:21, Rom 14:14, Ecc 9:10 and 2Cor 10:5 knowing stands beside a person's own thought: Moses fears the deed is known, Saul keeps Jonathan from knowing, Peter did not know the vision was real, those who knew God became futile in thinking, and every thought is brought under the knowledge of God. In Mat 22:16 and Mar 12:14 the questioners claim to know Jesus is true.
findings.grounds: although they knew God, they did not honor him
